a phrase: nind 'a finger' (reserve *niʔnd-) + strom 'great' (canon), noun and adjective, as many tongues name the thumb; no new root. V.7 I, Re hadhym et nind strom um et lodh, 'I put my thumb to the mortar'; unit S09

misk 'the foot' + S covv 'a cloak; wear' (c > h; compound: the head softened, §3.10), built exactly as biskhovv 'a hood ('head-cloak')' (O0093); no new root. V.7 III, pess ... o viskhovvath 'ask for his boots' (o + S: m > v); unit S09

drunn 'a mallet; a blow; strike' + S tolm 'a stone' (t > dh; compound: the head softened, §3.10), built as gorndholm 'cornerstone' and hessdholm 'boundary stone'; the smith's block, which the smith strikes as the mason strikes the chisel (Garvel 'little smith'); no new root. meanings: a jest ('a laughed thing'); laughed (the participle)

meanings: at the seat of; for, in the stead of (of one who speaks for the fallen at his seat by the fire): lo reskow Horlen 'for Corlen' ('at Corlen's seat')
derivation: a phrase: lo 'at, by' (+S; r unchanged) + reskow 'a place, a seat' (O2091, from resk 'sit'), the possessor after it softened as in any construct (Corlen > Horlen, Pellow > Vellow). Not ul reskow, which is the lexicon's 'somewhere' (O2636). The captions of VI.1 ('Voss, for Corlen'; 'Kael, for Hesk'; 'Ruan, for Pellow') and Kael's re wrodh ullen lo o reskow 'another spake for him': the living man sits in the dead man's seat at the haven's fire, as Kael 'sat at ten fires'; unit S09
